business_problem: Leyan Technology's intelligent customer-service robot had to route enormous amounts of dialog traffic for ecommerce brands, but the company's self-built Kafka environment was becoming expensive, hard to scale, and too inflexible for precision consumption. Because the same messaging backbone also served AI and data systems, instability or coarse-grained routing directly affected the performance and extensibility of its AI SaaS platform.
solution_summary: Leyan Technology rebuilt the messaging core behind its AI customer-service platform on Alibaba Cloud's serverless RocketMQ service. The new architecture keeps dialog distribution as the central event fabric for the LeYu Zhuren ecommerce robot, but replaces self-operated Kafka clusters with a managed message layer that can handle traffic spikes, resource elasticity, and differentiated delivery rules with less manual work. Messages from ecommerce conversations and downstream AI or data services are routed through RocketMQ topics and tags so consumer applications can subscribe with stronger precision than the earlier pipe-like design allowed. This gives Leyan a more cloud-native control plane for strong-consistency or ordered workloads, lowers the burden of operating multiple clusters, and preserves a reliable backbone for NLP, knowledge-graph, deep-learning, and large-model workloads that sit above the queue layer in its broader AI SaaS stack.

data_flow: Buyer requests from ecommerce channels enter Leyan's customer-service platform, are distributed through RocketMQ, and then consumed by AI dialog, recommendation, and data services. The processed outputs flow back into customer-service conversations or related downstream systems, while tags and filtering rules determine which business components consume which message streams.
business_outcome: Leyan lowered infrastructure cost for its AI service backbone while making the platform more adaptable for high-volume ecommerce support and new business scenarios. The RocketMQ-based redesign reduced overall cost by 37%, preserved support for a service that handles more than 20 million interactions per day, and gave the company a more precise and extensible messaging layer for both domestic and cross-border AI commerce services.
